predict_amber_onset — DRIVE decide op

• Data kinds: table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.predict_amber_onset(observations, *, flash_duration: 'Optional[float]' = None, crossing_length: 'Optional[float]' = None, walk_speed: 'float' = 1.0, ped_red_to_amber: 'float' = 2.0, t_now: 'Optional[float]' = None) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import drivedecide; drivedecide.predict_amber_onset(observations, *, flash_duration: 'Optional[float]' = None, crossing_length: 'Optional[float]' = None, walk_speed: 'float' = 1.0, ped_red_to_amber: 'float' = 2.0, t_now: 'Optional[float]' = None) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("predict_amber_onset"))

Usage

Estimates the start of the vehicle amber from observations of the parallel pedestrian signal ((t, state) in time order, state ∈ green / flash / red).

F = flash_duration (if absent, crossing_length / walk_speed), Δ = ped_red_to_amber. For each observed transition (green→flash, flash→red), an interval containing the amber time is formed, and their intersection is taken:

green→flash (last green t_g, first flash t_f): amber ∈ [t_g + F + Δ, t_f + F + Δ]

flash→red (last flash t_f', first red t_r): amber ∈ [t_f' + Δ, t_r + Δ]

Return value: amber_onset (midpoint of the interval), lo / hi, half_width (upper bound of the error), remaining = amber_onset − t_now (default = time of the last observation), basis (the transitions used). If there is not a single transition, ValueError (green merely continuing does not tell "when it will start flashing"). An empty interval (observations contradict F and Δ) is also ValueError.
